audit.whatIsWrong: The entry states Quinn's blind stops Tongue Lash: "the blind negates your slow" (mid) and "Blind Tongue Lash commits with Blinding Assault (Q) so Tahm Kench cannot land the slow" (wants.foe[1]).
audit.why: A blind in League causes basic attacks to miss. It has no effect on ability casts. Tongue Lash is a spell, so it lands, slows, heals and applies its An Acquired Taste stack while Tahm Kench is blinded. What Blinding Assault actually removes is the auto-attack half of his stacking, which is a different and more useful piece of advice.
audit.corrected: Blinding Assault blanks Tahm Kench's autos only; Tongue Lash still lands and still adds a stack through the blind.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry mentions that Behind Enemy Lines can be interrupted.
audit.why: Quinn's R is flagged channel/interruptible in the kit data, and _missing-interactions.json carries the row "Tahm Kench can cancel your Behind Enemy Lines (R) with Tongue Lash (Q)" for this exact pairing. Tongue Lash reaches 900 units, so a Quinn who casts her roam anywhere near the lane can simply be denied it. This is the single most actionable thing Tahm Kench does in this matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Tongue Lash cancels the Behind Enemy Lines take-off; punish the cast rather than trying to chase the roam.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quinn's ultimate is called "Behind the Scenes" in spikes[2], wants.foe[2] and whys[4].
audit.why: The real name is Behind Enemy Lines. Same error class as the calibration examples.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tahm Kench's own W is called "Abyssal Voyage" throughout and is treated as a level-6 global escape ("your pool animation", "use Abyssal Voyage to match her pressure").
audit.why: The live W is Abyssal Dive: a 1000-1200 range dive with a knockup, available from level 2, on 21/20/19/18/17. Abyssal Voyage was the pre-rework ally-carrying W and no longer exists. Every sentence treating it as a level-6 map tool is wrong twice over - wrong name, and wrong power level at the wrong time.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive (W), 1000-1200 range, knockup, up from level 2.

audit.whatIsWrong: Repeated claim that Quinn's Vault knockback "resets your 3-stack buildup" / "resets your An Acquired Taste stack count".
audit.why: Nothing in An Acquired Taste resets on displacement. The stacks simply expire on their own timer when Tahm Kench cannot reapply damage. Vault's real crime is that it leaves Quinn 675 units away, so the timer runs out. Same practical outcome, but a player told stacks are 'reset' will misplay the reapply window.
audit.corrected: Vault removes her from range so the existing stacks time out before you land the third.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere in the entry.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8 and is Quinn's only escape; Heightened Senses is 50s at rank 1. Those are the windows worth naming.
audit.corrected: Vault 12s at rank 1 is the punishable cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on the level chart. content win[] gives Quinn levels 1 through 6 and Tahm Kench only 2+ items; full phases[].side gives Quinn / Skill / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench / Quinn / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench.
audit.why: Tahm Kench is at 51.93% over 362 games, and the entry's own prose (spikes[3], whys[5]) says first item is his turning point while win[5] still reads Quinn. The full layer is closer to both the win rate and the prose.
audit.corrected: content win[5] should read Tahm Kench to match spikes[3], whys[5] and the full layer. Not proposed as an edit because a 5-char to 10-char swap cannot pass the +/-10% length gate.

edits.before: Quinn's Harrier passive procs a Vulnerable mark on you constantly — every empowered auto into her E vault knockback resets your 3-stack buildup and sends you stumbling backward with no gap-close answer.
edits.after: Quinn's Harrier mark procs on you constantly — her empowered auto into Vault (E) leaves her 675 units away, so the An Acquired Taste stacks you have already banked time out before you land the third.

edits.before: Behind the Scenes (R) turns Quinn into a roaming assassin — her global mobility eclipses your Abyssal Voyage and she will snowball sidelanes while you are stranded under tower farming.
edits.after: Behind Enemy Lines (R) turns Quinn into a roaming assassin, but the take-off is interruptible — a Tongue Lash inside your 900 range cancels it outright, so watch for the cast, not the exit.

edits.before: Survive lane to first item and accept that Quinn will roam — use Abyssal Voyage to match her pressure rather than chase her in the sidelane
edits.after: Survive to first item and punish her roams at the source — Tongue Lash the Behind Enemy Lines cast to cancel it instead of chasing her

edits.before: Blind Tongue Lash commits with Blinding Assault (Q) so Tahm Kench cannot land the slow and begin stacking An Acquired Taste
edits.after: Blind Tahm Kench with Blinding Assault (Q) so his autos whiff and Tongue Lash is his only An Acquired Taste source

edits.before: Roam constantly with Behind the Scenes (R) and force Tahm Kench to either follow with Abyssal Voyage or bleed out his turret
edits.after: Roam with Behind Enemy Lines (R), casting it outside Tongue Lash's 900 range so Tahm Kench cannot interrupt the take-off

edits.before: Quinn's Harrier passive empowered auto fires the instant lane starts and resets your An Acquired Taste stack count before Tongue Lash's slow can even land — you lose every level-1 trade.
edits.after: Quinn's Harrier empowered auto fires the instant lane starts and she steps out before you can add a second An Acquired Taste stack — the first expires and you lose every level-1 trade.

edits.before: Her Blinding Assault (Q) and Vault (E) knockback give her two independent ways to interrupt your 3-stack buildup before the Tongue Lash stun is ever online.
edits.after: Blinding Assault (Q) blanks your autos and Vault (E) pulls her out of range — two independent ways to stall your An Acquired Taste count at two rather than three.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage comes online but Quinn's Behind the Scenes (R) has always been a faster global — she will simply leave the lane and snowball a sidelane before your pool animation resolves.
edits.after: Devour arrives, but Abyssal Dive is only a 1000-unit hop rather than a map tool — Quinn's Behind Enemy Lines (R) leaves the lane and you have no way to match the pressure she makes.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Quinn's freest window. Without Abyssal Voyage you have zero escape if she commits, and with it on cooldown she can freely kite backward on Harrier move-speed whenever you try to fish for stacks in the open. Her Blinding Assault (Q) will punish any Tongue Lash you throw into open ground — the blind negates your slow and she resets to poke range before the debuff expires. Play tight to the wave, let her push into your turret occasionally, and bank your Thick Skin activation for when she commits a hard trade — converting your grey health to a shield right as her E vault lands denies her the chunking window she wants. At level 6 she will begin roaming with Behind the Scenes; ping immediately and recall or Abyssal Voyage to a threatened lane rather than duel her in a sidelane where Harrier's kite is unconstrained.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Quinn's freest window. Vault is 12 seconds at rank 1 and it is her only escape, so do not step past the wave for a third stack until you have watched her spend it. Blinding Assault does not stop Tongue Lash — a blind only makes basic attacks miss, so your Q still lands, still slows and still stacks while blinded; what you lose is the auto half of your stacking, so treat Q as your sole stack source until it drops. Play tight to the wave, let her push to your turret occasionally, and bank your Thick Skin activation for a hard trade — converting grey health to a shield as her Vault lands denies her the chunking window she wants. At level 6 she starts roaming with Behind Enemy Lines: if she casts inside your 900 range, Tongue Lash cancels the take-off; if she casts from further out, ping and rotate rather than duelling her in a sidelane.

edits.before: First item is your real turning point. Heartsteel's stacking aura or Sunfire's burn means your grey health regenerates faster than her sustained Harrier poke can deplete it, and a single clean Tongue Lash slow into 3-stack stun into Devour removes her from a teamfight entirely — Quinn has no answer for the Devour once she is stunned at melee range. At 2+ items you are the near-unkillable peeling machine and she is a high-priority glass cannon; lock her out of the backline with your W and her early lane lead becomes irrelevant. The caveat is vision and fog of war — Quinn in the lategame will pick off isolated allies with Harrier burst, so keep your Abyssal Voyage available to reposition and never let your backline walk into unwarded sidelanes without you nearby.
edits.after: First item is your real turning point. Heartsteel's stacking aura or Sunfire's burn means your grey health regenerates faster than her sustained Harrier poke can deplete it, and a single clean Tongue Lash slow into 3-stack stun into Devour removes her from a teamfight entirely — Quinn has no answer for the Devour once she is stunned at melee range. At 2+ items you are the near-unkillable peeling machine and she is a high-priority glass cannon; eject her from your backline with Devour and her early lane lead becomes irrelevant. The caveat is vision and fog of war — Quinn in the lategame will pick off isolated allies with Harrier burst, so hold Abyssal Dive to cross the last 1000 units and never let your backline walk unwarded sidelanes alone.

edits.before: - Quinn Vault: matchup-defining — Her self-peel. W-dive around it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Quinn Vault: matchup-defining — 12s at rank 1 and her only escape. Track it before every engage. - Her blind blanks autos, never Tongue Lash. - Devour needs 3 stacks: kill windows only.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Quinn's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour deletes her from the fight if you have 3 stacks. Her Behind Enemy Lines take-off is interruptible — Tongue Lash it.

notes: Champion-wide, not matchup-specific: champ-data/content/tahmkench.js contains 182 occurrences of 'Abyssal Voyage', which is the pre-rework W and does not exist on the live champion (W is Abyssal Dive, 1000-1200 range, knockup, 21/20/19/18/17, available from level 2). 'Abyssal Dive' appears 0 times in the file. Many of those occurrences also carry the wrong mechanical model - they describe it as a level-6 global/escape with a 'pool animation'. This needs a champion-wide sweep, not just my slice; a blind find-and-replace will fix the name but leave the wrong power level and wrong timing behind. champ-data/tahmkench.full.js is clean of the term. Also champion-wide: the full layer's templated strings use male pronouns for female enemies throughout ('Q-stun when his answer is down', 'zone Quinn off ... Dive with your jungler', 'Quinn carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides'). Not proposed as edits here since it is a generator-level issue across all 71 entries.
